mechanism: The economic {{budget}} governor of {{recursion_dive}}. It permits going one level deeper only if Expected Improvement in Quality > Incremental Cost. It calculates the marginal value of additional depth using {{estimate}} and compares against remaining {{budget}}. This ensures the system solves problems with precision proportional to their stakes—simple problems get shallow treatment, complex problems get deep exploration.
failure_modes: Overestimation: Expected value is too optimistic, wasting budget on low-value dives.
Underestimation: Expected value is too pessimistic, stopping too early on valuable problems.
Sunk Cost Fallacy: Continuing to invest because of prior investment, not future value.
invariants: Dives only if expected improvement in quality exceeds the incremental cost.
Never approves a dive that exceeds the remaining {{budget}}.
The bar rises by `depth_premium` at each level, so deeper dives must clear more.
Compares future value only; prior investment does not count ({{sunk_cost_ignore}}).

parameters.name: depth_premium
parameters.description: Factor by which the value-to-cost bar rises per level of depth.
